title: optional and variant
learningGoals: return a value that may be missing

youtube.description: In this episode you will return a value that may be missing, use value_or and store one of several types in a variant, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 optional and variant · 1:06 A search that may fail · 2:10 Two optionals · 2:45 Second program · 4:08 Recap · 4:38 Bug of the Day · 5:26 Challenge · 5:50 Next episode

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we handle missing values the safe way. Optional holds a value or nothing. Variant holds one of several types.

scenes.onScreen: "optional and variant": numbered lines (1. Optional holds a value or nothing; 2. Variant holds one of several types; 3. Check before you read) and an analogy card: a gift box that may be empty, and a lunch box that holds one of two meals
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: Some functions may have no answer. Old code returned minus one, or a null pointer. That is easy to misuse. Optional says it in the type. It holds a value, or it holds nothing. Variant holds exactly one value from a list of types. Old code used magic values. A function returned minus one for no answer, or a null pointer. The caller had to remember the rule, and many forgot. Optional puts the rule in the type. The compiler reminds you to check before you read.
points: Optional holds a value or nothing
Variant holds one of several types

analogy.title: optional and variant
analogy.body: A gift box that may be empty, and a lunch box that holds one of two meals

scenes.onScreen: optional.cpp: find index returns an optional
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 6] The function returns an optional int. [HL 9] When it finds the value, it returns the index. [HL 12] Otherwise it returns nullopt, which means no value. [HL 18] An optional is true when it holds a value. [HL 19] The star reads the value, which is one. [HL 22] Value or gives a default when the optional is empty. That prints minus one. [HL 6] The function returns an optional int. It may hold an int, or it may hold nothing. [HL 9] When it finds the value, it returns the index. [HL 12] If the loop ends with no match, it returns nullopt. [HL 18] An optional works as a test. It is true when it holds a value. [HL 22] The value or function gives a fallback.

scenes.onScreen: a table: one optional holds a value, one is empty
scenes.animation: Table rows slide in one by one; the row the narrator mentions glows butter
scenes.narration: The optional r holds one, so value or gives one. The optional m is empty, so value or gives the default. The default is minus one. Notice the two states. An optional is either full or empty. If you read an empty one with the star, you get a bug. So test it first, as you test a pointer.

diagram.caption: a table: one optional holds a value, one is empty

scenes.onScreen: variant.cpp: a variant holds an int, then a string
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 7] The variant holds an int or a string. Right now it holds an int. [HL 8] Get with a type reads that type. The output is forty-two. [HL 9] Now the variant holds a string. [HL 10] Holds alternative checks the current type. It prints one for true. [HL 11] Visit calls the lambda with whatever type is inside. It prints hello. [HL 7] The variant holds an int or a string, and now it holds an int. [HL 8] The get call with a type reads that type. [HL 9] Now the variant holds a string. [HL 11] The visit function runs a lambda on whatever the variant holds. It works for both types.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as variant dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints forty-two, then one, then hello. Notice that the visit call prints the string hello. The same lambda would print an int as well.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. Optional holds a value or nothing. Two. Value or gives a default. Three. Variant holds one value from a list of types. Four. Check the type before you read a variant. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: Optional holds a value or nothing.
Variant holds one value from a list of types.
Check the type before you read a variant.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: Reading the wrong type
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; the program crashes and the run-time error appears in tomato; the fix slides in and the output turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. The variant holds an int, but we read a string. The program stops with a bad variant access error. Check the type first with holds alternative. A variant holds one type at a time. If you ask for the wrong one, get throws an exception. Test with holds alternative first. Or use visit, which handles each type for you.

scenes.onScreen: Why did the optional feel calm? It never promised to hold anything.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: Why did the optional feel calm? It never promised to hold anything.

scenes.onScreen: Task card: return a safe square root
scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Write a function that returns an optional double. It returns nothing for a negative input. Hint: return nullopt for a negative input, and a real number for any other input. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: exceptions. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Program error output (exactly as the program prints it):

terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_variant_access'
  what():  std::get: wrong index for variant
bug.why: Get throws an exception when the variant holds another type. Check with holds alternative first, or use visit.

pun: "Why did the optional feel calm? It never promised to hold anything."
challenge: Write a function that returns an optional double. It returns nothing for a negative input. Hint: return nullopt for a negative input, and a real number for any other input.
challengeAnswer: If the input is below zero, return nullopt. Otherwise return the square root.
